To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the myocardial deoxy myoglobin resonance (Mb delta) intensity is an indicator of the intracellular PO2, and that during graded coronary hypoxemia, the intracellular oxygen tension required to maintain normal high energy phosphate levels in the in situ heart is less than 5 mmHog.

in the normal heart, the myocyte PO2 at which the intracellular high-energy phosphate (ATP and phosphocreatine [PCr]) levels are maintained is approximately 4 mmHg, which corresponds to a myoglobin oxygenation state of approximately 50%.
the myocardial PO(2) value required to sustain normal HEP levels is 5 mmH.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the role of myocardial oxygenation in the regulation of oxidative phosphorylating capacity in the intact heart.
the development and application of magnetic resonance (MR) techniques to study the regulation of myocardial oxygenation and energy metabolism.
the development of a non-invasive technique for monitoring myocardial oxygenation in vivo.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, in the in vivo canine heart, the myocyte PO2 values that are necessary to sustain normal HEP levels are approximately 5 mmHgg.
the PO(2) of the myocyte is a critical determinant in the maintenance of normal HEP levels in the in-vivo heart.
, in the normal canine heart, a reduction of myocardial blood flow from basal values to 20% of basal values is associated with a decrease of the mean myocyte PO( 2) from approximately 20 to 5 mmH 2.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
there is an intracellular PO( 2) threshold of about 5 mmH g that is necessary to maintain normal HEP levels.
the myocyte PO2 required to sustain normal HEP levels in the in-vivo heart is 5-6 mmHg.
the myocardial oxygenation threshold required to sustain normal levels of high-energy phosphate is in the 5 to 10 mmHg range.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the myocardium has an extremely high metabolic reserve and that the myocyte is able to maintain normal ATP and PCr levels during coronary hypoperfusion when intracellular PO2 values are above 5 mmHG, even when blood flow is reduced to approximately 30-40% of control values.
the myocardial PO2 required to sustain normal HEP levels is approximately 5 mmHog in vivo.
there is an inverse correlation between myocyte PO( 2) and the rate of ATP production in the in vivo canine heart.
